finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: the unauthenticated query parameter `host` is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, so shell metacharacters (;, &&, |, $(), backticks) execute arbitrary commands as the server user. Command output is also returned in the response.
finding.source: HTTP GET /ping?host=<value> — req.query.host, attacker-controlled, no authentication

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping registered with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated directly into the command string and passed to exec (shell)
stdout of the command is sent back to the caller, giving direct output exfiltration

finding.guards_checked: No input validation or allow-list on host; no escaping; no authentication or authorization middleware; app is only express() with no other middleware; exec is used (shell) rather than execFile with an args array. Also, req.query.host could be an array/object via qs parsing, which does not mitigate. A host value like `8.8.8.8; id` or `$(cat /etc/passwd)` works. /version uses execFile with fixed args and /uptime uses a constant string, so they are not injectable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to shell-based exec with no validation, auth middleware, or escaping, and tools.js:11 returns stdout. Output is only returned when the exit status is 0, but a payload like `8.8.8.8; id` exits 0 because the last command succeeds.
